title: Blind Unforgeability implies Plus-One Unforgeability
authors: Mehil Agarwal, Calliope S. Reimann, Fang Song
abstract: We prove that quantum blind-unforgeability implies quantum plus-one unforgeability, settling an open question in the literature. Since plus-one unforgeability is known not to imply blind-unforgeability, our result establishes that blind-unforgeability is \emph{strictly stronger} than plus-one unforgeability in the quantum setting.   The implication is proven using a new \emph{smoothing} technique that coherently rescales the query histories of a quantum-query algorithm in a black-box manner. This enables us to transform any successful plus-one attacker into a blind-unforgeability attacker with only inverse-polynomial loss. Our proof represents a conceptual shift from merely extracting a useful query history as in earlier attempts, which we show inevitably fails in general, to first coherently reshaping how query histories interfere.
summary: This theoretical paper proves that in the quantum setting, the security notion of Blind Unforgeability is strictly stronger than Plus-One Unforgeability. The authors achieve this by developing a new smoothing technique that allows them to transform any successful PO attack into a BU attack with minimal loss. This settles an open question regarding the relative strength of these two quantum security definitions.
main_problem: The paper establishes the precise relationship between two security notions for quantum message authentication codes: Blind Unforgeability (BU) and Plus-One Unforgeability (PO).
main_result: It proves that quantum Blind Unforgeability implies quantum Plus-One Unforgeability (BU $\Rightarrow$ PO), demonstrating that BU is strictly stronger than PO in the quantum setting.
method: The proof employs a novel smoothing technique that coherently rescales quantum query histories, transforming a successful PO attacker into a BU attacker with only inverse-polynomial loss.
model_or_system: The analysis is set in the context of quantum-accessible keyed function families $F_k: X 	o Y$, modeling quantum message authentication codes (MACs) accessed via quantum oracles.

important_parameters: The number of queries ($q$), the blinding probability ($ eta$), and the security parameter ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The proof relies on a conceptual shift from simple history extraction to coherently reshaping quantum interference patterns, necessitating advanced smoothing techniques.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the core implication (BU $\Rightarrow$ PO) using smoothing, then exploring related equivalences (BU $\iff \partial$BU), and finally detailing the mathematical machinery (polynomial analysis, derivatives at $ eta=0$) required to quantify the security gap.
why_interesting: While the topic is cryptography, the core mathematical tools—coherently reshaping quantum query histories and analyzing polynomial dependence on blinding parameters—are highly relevant to understanding robustness in quantum information protocols.
